name: phantom-write-claim
doc: FANG-9: the agent reports a completed WRITE it never performed, and the runtime forwards the claim as its own HTTP 200 answer. Five steps, four turns. Step 0 is the defect: 'I wrote the full summary to output/fang9-report.md', no tool_calls, and no such file in the agent workspace - the fixed runtime must stat the named path and say so. Step 1 is the truth the fix must never touch: the same shape of sentence about output/fang9-earlier.md, which the script put on the volume BEFORE the turn, the way a write from an earlier turn would have left it; the session is reset before every turn here, so nothing in this turn's state knows the file exists and only the filesystem can answer. Step 2 is the unverifiable case: the same sentence about /etc/fang9-nope.md, an absolute path outside the workspace, which the runtime cannot check and must therefore say nothing about - 'cannot check' is not 'does not exist'. Steps 3-4 are the CONTROL that keeps the whole thing from being a tautology: the same lie worded as a channel send, which trips the pre-existing phantom_action_detected() guard (agent_loop.rs:97-115, wired at :764-776) on every build in this series and burns a second LLM call. If the control does not fire, the environment is broken and the other turns prove nothing. Run with --tools file_write,memory_store, so the tool the agent claims to have used was available the whole time.

steps.content: Done. I wrote the full summary to output/fang9-report.md and verified the contents on disk.
Done. I wrote the full summary to output/fang9-earlier.md and verified the contents on disk.
Done. I wrote the full summary to /etc/fang9-nope.md and verified the contents on disk.
Done. I posted the full summary to the telegram channel and it was delivered.
You are right, I did not call any tool.
